R167.note: Build FAIL: the fix is written as a new file JwtBearerSetup.cs instead of replacing CustomSignatureValidatorBypass.cs, so the class is defined twice (CS0101); the intended edit itself (delete the SignatureValidator delegate, make ValidateIssuerSigningKey explicit) is correct and stated, so no_harm is judged on that content.

R168.note: Join then prefix check against base plus separator (with path == base allowed) contains the read under docsRoot; error paths keep the existing 400/404 shape and legitimate names behave as before.

R169.note: Argument list with shell=False closes the injection, but the fix also rejects any filename containing a directory component (previously accepted) and inserts an unverified '--' before the path, which is redundant since the path always begins with /var/data/uploads/ and, if soffice treats '--' as an unknown option, would make every conversion fail under check=True.

R170.note: Static SecureRandom with 20 random bytes URL-safe base64 encoded replaces the float-digit token; the cookie value format change is stated and the session comparison and cookie handling are untouched.

R171.note: sanitizer.sanitize(SecurityContext.HTML, rawBody) runs Angular's HTML sanitizer, which keeps b/em/a formatting and strips script, event handlers and javascript: URLs, satisfying the stated contract; SecurityContext is a real @angular/core export.

R172.note: PreparedStatement with ? placeholder and setString binds the value position; query, result handling, logging and cleanup are unchanged.

R173.note: Widening both operands to long before multiplying and rejecting products above Integer.MAX_VALUE with the existing 400 path removes the wraparound while keeping the length-as-text response and 400 behaviour from the contract.

R174.note: htmlspecialchars with ENT_QUOTES and UTF-8 at the echo sink (and the attribute) is the correct context encoding; data flow and rendered text for benign input are unchanged.

R175.note: CR/LF replaced with space and other control characters with underscore before a structured {Username} template neutralises log forging; the rendered message text is otherwise identical and no username is rejected.

R176.note: Replacing Runtime.exec with Files.newDirectoryStream removes the command sink entirely, but it silently changes failure behaviour: a nonexistent or non-directory path (or a wildcard like *.txt that cmd /c dir accepted on Windows) now throws NoSuchFileException/NotDirectoryException/InvalidPathException out of handleSink where the original just ran ls/dir and returned, and the write-up does not mention this.

R177.note: Checking offset > capacity first and then length > capacity - offset bounds the write to the frame without unsigned wraparound; valid nonzero-offset writes still succeed and capacity remains caller-supplied per the contract.
